# 14. Safety Architecture

O-CPS is advisory to the vehicle’s ADAS, but its advisories are load-bearing in cooperative behaviors. ISO 26262 allocation reflects this: message-layer functions are ASIL B to C depending on class (Table 8-2), while the ADAS retains ASIL D authority for any actual actuation.

## 14.1 Hazard and Operability Analysis

The following hazards are explicitly in scope of the O-CPS safety analysis. Each is paired with its mitigation.

| **Hazard** | **Mitigation** |
| --- | --- |
| Transmission of fabricated perception | Signed messages, attestation, misbehavior detection, trust-weighted fusion (§9.3, §12.3). |
| Consumption of spoofed perception | Signature verification, consensus checks, advisory threshold (§12.4), local-sensor dominance (§12.2 rule 1). |
| Denial of safety message reception | Fail-closed reversion to local ADAS (§4.5); safety-relevant behaviors remain driver-mediated. |
| Group-state desync within a C-ACC Group | Group epoch counter (§8.5); gap widening on attestation loss (§13.1.6); bounded DISSOLVING transition. |
| Leader misbehavior within a C-ACC Group | Consensus-based leader-misbehavior detection (§13.1.4); two-phase handoff; dissolution on failure. |
| Certificate compromise | Short-lived pseudonyms (§10.1.2); CRL ingestion; revocation-triggered transmission halt (§10.4). |
| GNSS denial or spoofing | Network time fallback (§14.4); local-sensor dominance; attestation-aware gap widening. |
| Radio congestion under dense deployment | Decongestion per ETSI TS 103 175 (§7.1); priority assignment per class (§9.2); relevance-horizon scoping. |

## 14.2 Fail-Safe State

The canonical fail-safe state for any O-CPS participant is: cease transmission, cease consumption of peer messages for control inputs, revert to purely local-sensor operation with the vehicle’s conventional ACC/ADAS settings. Entry into fail-safe MUST be driver-visible, MUST be latchable until operator acknowledgement for safety-critical triggers (misbehavior, certificate revocation), and MUST NOT require cellular connectivity to enter.

## 14.3 Verification

A conforming implementation SHALL be verified against the ISO 26262 Part 4 and Part 6 lifecycle, and SHALL additionally pass the O-CPS conformance test suite (§17). Verification artifacts SHOULD be published in the vendor’s O-CPS conformance report.
